summary: High 5xx rate from pipelined embedding uploads causing API gateway saturation and upstream runtime OOMs
description: Issue summary: Customers are observing a sustained spike of 5xx responses from the Redwood API gateway beginning 2026-03-12 17:20 UTC. The traffic pattern correlates with large, pipelined embedding uploads from a single high-throughput tenant (CortexMaps). Upstream serving runtimes are reporting OOMs and repeated process restarts, and the API gateway shows connection queue growth and SIGPIPE errors.
impact: Multiple API calls for embeddings fail with 502/503/504. Customer reports ~40% of embedding requests failing in us-east during the window. Downstream application retries caused cascading load; several internal alerts fired for runtime OOMs and apigw accept-queue depth.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Use CortexMaps account credentials to upload embeddings in parallel with pipelined HTTP/2 streams (100 concurrent streams, large payloads ~40MB each).
2) Observe elevated 5xx rate on POST /v1/embeddings and repeated runtime restarts in the same availability pool.
3) Reduce concurrency and note errors reduce proportionally.
observed_logs:
[2026-03-12T17:23:10Z] apigw: accept_queue=1240 backlog=1024 conn_reset=12
[2026-03-12T17:23:12Z] runtime: process=serving-312 pid=4211 OOM-kill signal received, kv_cache_evictions=high
[2026-03-12T17:23:14Z] apigw: error writing upstream: broken pipe (SIGPIPE)
[2026-03-12T17:24:02Z] scheduler: ephemeral-worker-throttle triggered for pool us-east-a
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Large pipelined uploads are saturating apigw socket buffers and accept queues, causing slow upstream responses and backpressure to the serving runtime. Hypothesis 2: The serving runtime's KV cache and allocator are being pressured by many large embedding batches, causing memory fragmentation and eventual OOMs. Evidence: kernel network buffers and accept queue metrics spike in the same host pool; NVMe iowait is nominal. Attempts to repro in staging with synthetic load show similar accept-queue growth when payloads > 20MB and > 50 concurrent streams. Observed that evictions climb and runtime memory footprint grows with concurrency and pipelining depth.
mitigation_steps_taken:
1) Applied temporary ingress rate limit for CortexMaps tenant at 300 RPS and throttled concurrent streams per connection.
2) Routed new CortexMaps traffic to a warmed dedicated pool with higher memory headroom.
3) Increased apigw accept-queue and tuned SO_RCVBUF on affected frontends as short-term relief.
Result: 5xx rate dropped from ~40% to ~6% within 15 minutes after throttling and routing change.
next_steps:
1) Engineering to implement per-tenant max-pipelined-streams enforcement in apigw (PR drafted).
2) Runtime team to add guardrails around large-batch allocations to fail-fast for oversized embedding payloads.
3) Create automated test covering pipelined-large-payload failure mode in CI.
4) Follow-up postmortem and update customer-facing recommendations for maximum concurrency/payload size.
resolution: Mitigation deployed: tenant throttling and temporary routing to warmed pool. Engineering changes planned; ticket remains open until durable fixes are merged and deployed.
